subject: Load Testing & Acceptance Plan for Acme Payments - Benchmarks and Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jorlee@acmepay.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Load testing & acceptance plan — Redwood x Acme Payments

Hi Jordan / Acme team,

Thanks again for kicking off onboarding with us. As we discussed in the kickoff, the next milestone is the formal acceptance test so we can sign off on SLA targets and move to production traffic routing. Attached is the first draft of the "Load Test & Acceptance Plan" (acme_load_test_plan_v1.pdf). Key items summarized below: 

- Acceptance criteria (proposal):
  - P95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250 ms for single-turn generate requests at 50 req/s sustained
  - 99th percentile latency for 1k-token completions < 1.2s when batching is enabled
  - Throughput: sustain 10k tokens/sec aggregate across the dedicated pool for 30 min
  - Error rate (5xx/timeout) < 0.1% during test window
- Load profile: warmup 10 min, stepped load (10 -> 25 -> 50 -> 75 req/s), 10 min steady at each step
- Test environment: Redwood Dedicated staging cluster (us-west), dataset: anonymized production-ish prompt set you provided
- Success sign-off: Acme CS + Redwood SRE + product owner sign off on metrics and any regressions

Next actions: please confirm the acceptance criteria above and share any additional constraints (IP allow lists, max parallel users, tokens/req expectations). If that looks good, can we lock a test window for next Tue/Wed (Feb 24/25)?

Attachments: acme_load_test_plan_v1.pdf (PDF with test matrix and measurement), sample load_test_script.jmx (JMeter), runbook_onboarding.md

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0102

From: Jordan Lee <jorlee@acmepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmepay.com>, onboarding@acmepay.com
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:02:18 -0500
Subject: Re: Load testing & acceptance plan — Redwood x Acme Payments

Hi Marissa — thanks for the doc and clear checklist. A few notes from our side: 

- The targets look reasonable. A couple of constraints to call out: our production traffic peaks are roughly ~65 req/s for the checkout flow (short prompts ~60-80 tokens). We can spare 50 req/s from a replica pool for the acceptance run but we'd like to see a plan to demonstrate headroom to 75 req/s.
- Token limits: our longest expected completion is ~1500 tokens for dispute summaries — if you can include a sample 1k–1.5k token run in the plan that would be ideal.
- Security: we'll need the IP ranges for your dedicated test instances and the SAML test identity for auth; I'll follow up with the SSO admin.

Proposed schedule: Wed Feb 25, 10:00–12:00 PT for the primary run, with a contingency slot on Thu Feb 26. Please confirm if Redwood can run both the short (60–80 token) and long (1k–1.5k token) scenarios in the same window.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Lead Platform Engineer, Acme Payments
jorlee@acmepay.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Requests: 
- Priyom: can you prepare two test profiles: (A) short-turn profile (60–80 tokens) at stepped load up to 75 req/s, (B) long-completion profile (1k–1.5k tokens) at up to 25 req/s. Please include both an unquantized and an int8/quantized run so we can compare latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Stephanie: please confirm SRE on-call and make sure we have IP whitelist + SAML test account ready (Jordan will provide SSO admin contact).
- Rishi: we may need manager-level sign-off on enabling extra burst capacity in Dedicated staging for the headroom run — can you approve a temporary 48-hour bump?

I'll coordinate with Acme to lock the window once we confirm infra. Priyom, can you aim to have scripts and a dry run by Mon 23rd?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jorlee@acmepay.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Results: Acceptance run complete — Redwood x Acme Payments (summary + artifacts)

Hi Jordan / Sasha —

Thanks for running with us today. Summary of the acceptance run and artifacts attached below. Full artifacts are in the attachments and the Grafana dashboard link.

Quick summary (Wed Feb 25, 10:00–11:45 PT):
- Short-turn profile (60–80 tokens): sustained 50 req/s baseline, stepped up to 75 req/s. P95 latency at 75 req/s = 238 ms (meets target). Error rate during steady-state = 0.03%.
- Long-completion profile (1k–1.5k tokens): ran at 20–25 req/s. P95 for long completions = 980 ms; 99th = 1.08 s. Throughput during long run averaged 9.6k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Quantized vs baseline: int8 quantized variant reduced median latency by ~12% for short-turns, with a ~7% increase in token generation variance for long completions. No functional regressions observed in the evaluation prompt set.
- Resource notes: temporary +30% burst on Dedicated staging used during headroom step; CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit-rate are in the dashboard.

Attachments: acme_load_test_results_20260225.csv (CSV with time-series metrics), load_test_script.jmx, runbook_onboarding.md
Grafana (live): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ABc123/acme-load-tests
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/view/RDW-ACME-2026-045

Next steps: 
- Acme: please review the attached CSV and confirm whether the observed headroom and quantization tradeoffs are acceptable for production rollout.
- Redwood: we'll prepare a short technical note outlining the recommended configuration for production (batching, cache TTL, and quantization profile) and a proposed cutover plan.

If Acme signs off, we'll move to schedule a production cutover for a phased roll starting Mar 4.

Best regards,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
